steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 loaf pans; sprinkle 1 teaspoon sugar onto the bottom and sides of the greased pans.

Beat 2 cups sugar, oil, eggs, lemon zest, lemon extract, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl until well combined. Whisk flour, salt, baking soda, and baking powder together in a separate bowl until well mixed; add to sugar-lemon mixture and stir until batter is thick. Fold in zucchini until incorporated. Divide batter between the prepared pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into centers comes out clean, about 1 hour. Cool loaves in the pans for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Ellen's Lemon Zucchini Bread
raw_recipe.description: Lemon zest and lemon extract give this zucchini bread recipe an extra boost of citrus flavor.

review.reviewBody: My boyfriend and I LOVE this recipe. It's one of the best breads we've ever made. We actually halved the recipe to get one loaf. Also, lemon extract can be substituted with lemon juice (rule of thumb is 3x amount of extract called for, i.e. 3 teaspoons of lemon juice for 1 teaspoon of lemon extract). The dusted sugar on the pan gives a nice crisp, but sweet outside, while the zucchini makes the inside super moist!

I really enjoyed this bread. It's moist and lemony. This freezes well . It makes four small loaves with a 35 minute cook time at 350. Two teaspoons of lemon extract and juice of half a lemon makes it extra lemony. This is my favorite zucchini bread recipe.

This was highly appreciated by my guys. I followed the recipe almost exactly, except I added 3/4 c. raisins and 3/4 c. chopped walnuts, because my buddy asked me to. I did not have lemon extract, so I used the juice from the lemon I zested. The lemon flavor was perfect, not too strong or too weak. It complemented the zucchini perfectly. The batter was so thick I thought I had accidentally put too much flour in, but it came out lovely. moist and yummy. I didn't have 2 loaf pans, so I made 18 cupcakes and a loaf. Alghough they only lasted a day and a half at my house, the bread stayed very moist. Thanks for a great recipe, Ellen.

This one is a keeper ! The changes I made were to use half the oil and the rest applesauce, no extract (I don't like extracts) added juice from zested lemon. Also I used 1 cup strawberry jelly in place of one cup sugar. Adding jello lemon pudding made this rise nicely. Baked in a big rectangle baking dish and will spread cream cheese frosting over top.
Be sure to keep an eye on this towards end of baking, it may take less time.

I add finely chopped lavender, used 1 cup granulated sugar/stevia, 2 cups wholewheat flour (ground in Vitamix) /1 cup all purpose. Added the juice of the lemon as well as the lemon extract, makes 12 muffins. Outstanding!

Subbed out with the following:
Instead of oil: 1/2 cup veg oil + 1/2 cup apple sauce
2 tsp cinnamon
2 tsp vanilla extract
Instead of lemon extract: 3 Tbsp lemon juice
2 lemons zested
3 shredded zucchinis
added chopped walnuts

It was a bit sweet - next time perhaps cut some of the sugar?

This lemon zucchini bread is absolutely wonderful. I did not have any lemon extract so I substituted 2 tablespoons of fresh lemon juice. You could definitely taste the lemon in the bread but it was not overpowering. I also baked it in small bread pans, the recipe made four pans filled about 3/4 full. I baked it for 40 minutes at 350. I sprayed the pan with cooking spray made for baking, that stuff works beautifully.
I doubled the lemon extract and vanilla like some one suggested awesome taste best I ever made love it made 3 times, been sharing with my friends passed the recipe on twice now. 😋

I've tried countless zucchini breads and this is one of the best. I only made one loaf using 2 eggs. Be sure to use lemon extract and not lemon juice for the ultimate lemon flavor. I also drizzled it with an icing of confectioner's sugar and lemon juice. It's a keeper!

I made this yesterday and made some tweaks. It came out perfectly and I'm a serious baker. I used 1/2c canola oil and 1/2 c applesauce. I added 2 tsp cinnamon, increased vanilla to 2tsp, used 3T lemon juice instead of extract, 2 lemons zested, and 2 c regular flour and 1c white whole wheat flour. I used 3c shredded zucchini instead of 2. Best bread I've made so far.

I got lots of compliments on this bread with a few changes. I used all whole wheat flour with great results. I used Truvia Baking Blend to replace all sugar. In place of all the oil, I used 1.4 cup oil and 3.4 cup unsweetened applesauce. Will make many more times!
great

Excellent bread! I made one change only because I ran out of sugar. I decided to make it anyway as I had already prepped everything. The sugar in the pan idea I had never tried but I think this made the bread sweet enough for my taste as we didn’t miss the extra 1/2 cup of sugar I was missing. Also, I used up frozen lemon zest I had previously grated waiting for a recipe like this. This bread is delicious & very moist.
This is so good. I followed the recipe exactly and written.
So moist and lemony!!!
We love these. I usually make muffins because the grandkids love to grab one and go! They are a really nice muffin!

If I had never tasted lemon bread, or zucchini bread, I would like this recipe. However, I have baked both of those delicious breads, and I think this bread is an awkward combination of the two better sweet breads. It is lemon bread with a vegetable overtone. 

Not a favorite at our house.

I have officially found my absolute FAVORITE Zucchini bread-right HERE!! I've made countless bread recipes with all the zucchini from my garden, & THIS one is the B-O-M-B-!-! I did add a TBSP of lemon juice from the lemon I zested, along with the lemon extract. I made 1 regular & 2 small loaves, & after dinner tonite I'm gonna make another batch to give to family. My search for the most EPIC zucchini bread is OVER! -TY!!

Excellent! We love Ellen's Lemon Zucchini Bread. Thank you for the recipe. I wasn't sure what the intention was for the lemon, so I added the juice (2 tbsp.) in addition to the zest. Next time I'll also add an additional tsp. of lemon extract.
Love it my go too! This has so many great flavors in this recipe! Thanks for sharing!
